title: Cliffs striped red and white
text: The cliffs of Red Rock Canyon State Park get their vivid colors from alternating layers of white clay and red sandstone. The park covers about 27,000 acres along Highway 14, about 25 miles northeast of Mojave. In the early 1870s, its colorful formations served as landmarks for twenty-mule-team freight wagons. The area was once home to the Kawaiisu people. The state park was created in 1968.
